newsitem.title: UK: UK 1997 house prices to rise 6-8 pct - Halifax.
newsitem.headline: UK 1997 house prices to rise 6-8 pct - Halifax.

text.p: The recovery in the British housing market, firmly established in 1996, will gather pace in 1997 with prices set to rise by up to eight percent, the Halifax Building Society said on Tuesday.
"We are forecasting prices will rise by between six and eight percent next year with the outcome more likely to be in the upper end of the range," a spokesman said.
This compares with house price rises of around seven percent in 1996. Transactions are forecast to rise by 10 percent during 1997 compared with seven percent in 1996.
Planned tax cuts announced in the November budget will help boost housing market activity and prices.

"The announced cuts in personal taxation will result in growth in real personal disposable incomes of up to 3.0 percent in 1997 and should sustain the housing upturn," the Halifax said in its housing market review.
The prospect of higher interest rates casts a shadow over the market. But as long as any further rate rises are modest, the recovery should continue.

"Interest rates in the UK are clearly on the upward part of the interst rate cycle, but as long as rises in 1997 are only moderate -- bank base rates, for example, ending the year at seven to eight percent -- then this should not prevent further steady growth in both housing transactions and house prices," the Halifax said.
Along with higher interest rates, the high level of outstanding personal debt will ensure the housing market does not return to the boom conditions seen in the late 1980s.

"Overall levels of mortgage debt are at higher levels now than they were in the 1980s. As long as overall levels of inflation are kept at low levels, then significantly higher growth in house prices would seem unlikely."
